items.name: Distributed data-parallel training
items.description: Editable data-parallel training figure composing the dataset, gpu, and server icons: a training-data source shards batches to GPU workers that exchange gradients and weights with a parameter server. Parametric spacing and labels.

items.name: Model inference serving
items.description: Editable deployment figure composing the cloud, server, gpu, and database icons: client requests flow over the internet through a load balancer to GPU-backed inference nodes that read from a feature store, with a dashed inference-cluster boundary. Parametric spacing and labels.

items.name: Agent Tool-Use Stack (MCP)
items.description: LLM agent tool-use stack with brand logos: user to an LLM core to MCP servers fanning out to swappable tool cards.

items.name: Aurora storage node IO (Verbitski et al.)
items.description: IO traffic inside an Amazon Aurora storage node, redrawn after Figure 4 of Verbitski et al., SIGMOD 2017: eight numbered steps from receiving log records and acknowledging them, through sorting, peer gossip and coalescing into data pages, to S3 backup, garbage collection and scrubbing.

items.name: CLIP method overview (Radford et al.)
items.description: Three-panel overview of CLIP redrawn after Figure 1 of Radford et al., ICML 2021: contrastive pre-training with the N by N similarity matrix, a dataset classifier built from label text, and zero-shot prediction. The original photographs are replaced by neutral placeholders.

items.name: Encoder-decoder (bottleneck)
items.description: Block-level encoder-decoder 'hourglass': input block, encoder trapezoid narrowing to a latent bottleneck z, decoder trapezoid widening to an output block. Parametric sizes and labels.

items.name: Feed-forward neural network
items.description: Parametric fully-connected feed-forward neural network. Layer count and neurons-per-layer are set by a single list at the top of the file.

items.name: Flowchart (decision + loop)
items.description: Standard flowchart: terminal pills (start/end), process rectangles, a decision diamond with Yes/No branches, and a retry loop. Parametric spacing and labels.

items.name: LLM Serving Stack
items.description: LLM inference serving stack with brand logos: users to a vLLM engine on a GPU cluster, serving swappable model cards.

items.name: ResNet residual block
items.description: The classic ResNet residual learning building block (He et al.): a stack of weight layers forming F(x), an identity skip connection that re-enters at a summation node, and a final activation. The number of weight layers is driven by a single list at the top of the file.

items.name: System block diagram
items.description: General system architecture diagram: external client, process boxes (gateway/services), datastore cylinders (database/cache), branching connections, and a dashed subsystem group box. Multiple component types, parametric spacing.

items.name: Transformer architecture (Vaswani et al.)
items.description: Full encoder-decoder Transformer redrawn after Figure 1 of Vaswani et al., NeurIPS 2017: embeddings and positional encodings, the repeated encoder and decoder stacks with residual connections, the encoder memory feeding the decoder's middle attention, and the Linear and Softmax output head.

items.name: FlashAttention (IO-aware attention)
items.description: FlashAttention, three-panel homage after Dao et al., 2022. Left: the GPU memory hierarchy as a banded triangle (SRAM 19 TB/s / HBM 1.5 TB/s / DRAM 12.8 GB/s) showing the bandwidth-vs-size trade-off. Center: the IO-aware dataflow — Q, K^T and V tiles streamed from HBM, copied block-by-block into SRAM (outer loop over K/V, inner loop over Q), where the QK^T block and softmax are fused before sm(QK^T)V is written back to HBM. Right: the GPT-2 attention runtime, a stacked PyTorch bar (Matmul/Mask/Softmax/Dropout/Matmul) versus FlashAttention's single fused kernel.

items.name: Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)
items.description: Block-level GAN overview: a low-dimensional latent bar feeds the generator G (expanding trapezoid) producing generated fake images, while a high-dimensional sample-space stack supplies real images; both feed the discriminator D (compressing trapezoid) that outputs a real/fake decision. Parametric sizes, colors, and labels.

items.name: LoRA (low-rank adaptation)
items.description: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA), two-panel homage after Hu et al., 2021. During training: a frozen pretrained weight W feeds Wx in parallel with a trainable low-rank update B·A (rank-r bottleneck, A=N(0,sigma^2), B=0) feeding BAx, summed to h. After training: the adapter is folded into a single merged weight matrix W_merged, shown as a bar–square–bar stack. Center column gives h = Wx + BAx = (W + BA)x.
